units.translation: And he oversees everything with a tablet-writing mind.
Because Persuasion watches over my tongue and mouth.
a place from which something is observed
a place from which something is observed
Said of Argus guarding Io. The scholiast did not understand, who explains it by κατανομάς [pastures].
the flowery pastures of my mother
But my fate, reaching to heaven, falls to the ground.
to come as quickly as possible, lovely to the city
A verb form not known from elsewhere.
being a poor man, to desire marriage with one of those exalted by birth
The passive aorist form ἠράσθην [I fell in love] is frequent among the Attics with active meaning, on which see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1967.
The holy heaven longs to pierce the earth.
For Death alone of the gods does not love gifts.
(with perfect εἴργασμαι [I have done], which is used both actively and passively, and aorist εἰργασάμην [I did]) to accomplish, to bring about
You have done this incredible thing.
Or many evils have been done by me in the house.
For a grace not without honor has been achieved through toils.
The deed seems to me to have been done.

where now ἐργάνην [worker] has been restored from Stobaeus, which could also have been in M, in which the last letters άτιν [worker] have been written by a more recent hand over an erasure of the old writing. On the word ἐργάνη [worker] see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1971.

and the combinations of letters (rightly σύνθεσιν [composition], which Stobaeus Flor. 81, 1, although in not the best manuscripts), the mother of the Muses, worker of memory (thus Hemsterhuis for μνήμην [memory]) of all things (ἐργάτην [worker] in many copies)
Some wrath will come upon these deeds.
work, labor, deed, matter at hand
work, labor, deed, matter at hand
It is of rarer use when said of the procreation of children.
ἔργῳ [in deed] is not rarely opposed to ἔπος [word], λόγος [speech], μύθος [tale].
in a corrupt passage, in which ἔργῳ [in deed], which the scholiast does not seem to have read, has undoubtedly been introduced from the preceding verse.
i.e. in reality, as in others λόγῳ [in word] and ἔργῳ [in deed] or ἔργοις [in deeds], on which see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1982.
This deed is being accomplished and is not in vain.
And indeed the deed has been done.
The one who assesses the deeds is harsh.
Ares will decide the work by dice.
whoever assigned this task to the shield
Or is such a deed also dear to the gods?
Justice was present in his deeds and thoughts.
But this deed was against all instead of one.
Therefore for them a very great deed has been accomplished.
For the impious deed begets more.
The deed seems to me to have been done.
